concept: Tray is a recess pressed into a dial unit that gathers its small secondary keys, such as previous, next, a mode key and a lamp, into one place. With the small keys sunk together in one tray, the unit's one big orange part stands alone on the plastic, the way a recessed key tray sits beside the main knob of a synthesiser.

default_to_avoid.pattern: toolbar or ButtonGroup of outlined buttons joined edge to edge, used as a tray of secondary keys
default_to_avoid.why_not: P1 makes the loud control the one largest part with smaller keys beside it, so the small keys sink into a recess instead of forming a second raised bank as wide as the knob.

default_to_avoid.pattern: tray drawn as a bordered box or a card inside the card
default_to_avoid.why_not: P4 keeps every hole a recess with inverse light, so the tray is pressed into the plastic, never a raised panel or a hairline box.

references.source: Sytren synthesiser: a recessed tray groups the small keys so the main control stands alone
Braun T 1000 world receiver and Braun audio units (Dieter Rams): small keys set together in one recessed field beside the large tuning knob
packages/react/src/components/Display (dial): the recessed window whose corner nests in the body (inner = outer − inset)

derivation.consequence: the loud control is the one round or largest part; secondary controls are smaller keys
derivation.form: The tray holds only the 44px keys, the small capsule keys and the lamps, so the knob or the big orange key beside it stays the largest part.

derivation.consequence: the loud control gets the largest clear area in the unit and sits where the hand expects it (lower or right of the display)
derivation.form: Gathering the small keys into one tray clears the plastic around the loud part, which keeps its own clear area at the end of the row.

derivation.consequence: each hole is a recess (inverse light), never a printed dot
derivation.form: The tray is a recess with the well's inverse light, the same kind of hole as the display window, and the keys stand up from its floor.

derivation.consequence: the window is a rounded rectangle whose radius nests in the body (inner = outer − inset)
derivation.form: The tray takes the display window's nested corner, outer radius minus the body's inset, so the unit has one family of recesses.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The tray never shrinks its keys: each child keeps its own size, and the tray wraps to a second row instead.

options.name: recess on the inset line: one well with the display window's nested corner and even insets, wrapping to rows
capsule well: round ends wrapped on the round keys
seamed bank: the keys joined into one raised strip

variants.reason: A shares the display window's nested corner and recess (P2, P4), so the unit has one family of holes, and it wraps without changing shape; B reads as a segmented pill and cannot wrap, and C is the ButtonGroup, a second raised part competing with the knob (P1).

root.why: The tray is one recess with the well's inverse light and an even inset all round, holding the small keys on its floor.

data-component=Badge.why: A lamp printed at the tray's end keeps the even inset from the tray's edge, so its word never touches the recess wall.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the tray keeps a hairline outline, because the recess shading that draws it fades there.
